meta.title: Products
meta.description: Eleven apps for your company and for you: CRM, Chat, Agents, Flow, Robots, Track, Link, Docs, Notes, Cal and Board. Open source to run on your server, or in our cloud with a free plan to start.

hero.sub: The tools that run a company — customers, support, automations, AI agents, tasks, links — and the ones you use alone: notes, docs, whiteboards, your calendar. We rebuilt them in the open. The core costs zero and it is yours.

compare.note: Self-hosted: every month, every year, forever. On Zerosoft Cloud you start free and pay only for what scales.

i1.name: Link · CRM · Docs · Chat
i1.what: Short links, pipelines, a block-editor wiki and a support inbox. Live and free.

i2.name: Track · Cal

i3.name: Connect
i3.what: API and webhooks for Track. Outlook and iCloud calendars for Cal.

cta.sub: All of them are live and free to start. Get in now: you pay only for what scales.

meta.title: Link — Short links, free forever
meta.description: Custom domains, real analytics, QR codes, link-in-bio, Bitly import, webhooks and a public API. The Bitly alternative that costs zero.

hero.sub: Everything Bitly charges $35 a month for — custom domains, click analytics, QR codes, link-in-bio, a real API and webhooks — rebuilt, open sourced and set free. Already live.

f1.d: go.yourcompany.com/slug. Add the DNS record, verify, done — HTTPS is automatic on our cloud. Same slug on different domains, and you choose where the bare domain goes.

f2.d: Clicks by day, referrer, country, device, browser and OS. 7, 30, 90 days or all time, compared with the previous period. Cookie-less, fingerprint-less, honest.

f3.d: Every link gets an instant QR in SVG or PNG. Print it, project it, ship it.

f4.d: Lock a link with a password. Set an expiry date or a maximum click count. The link retires itself.

f5.d: Paste a Bitly API token to bring the whole account, or upload the CSV export. Back-halves stay. Verify your domain here first and old links keep working when you move the DNS.

f6.d: One page at zerosoft.ai/@you. Pick your links, put them in order, share it. Every click still counts.

f7.d: Tag links by campaign, client or channel. Build UTM URLs without a spreadsheet. Find anything in seconds.

f8.d: Create and measure links from your code with REST API v1. Get link.created and link.clicked as signed webhooks, with retries.

f9.d: Every link as CSV. Every click as JSON. Or pull it all through the API. No hostages.

compare.note: Bitly Core costs $35 a month — $420 a year, every year. A 10-person team on per-seat pricing easily crosses $4,200 a year. Self-hosted Link costs $0. Forever.

f1.a: Yes. The core is open source (AGPLv3) and self-hosting costs nothing, forever. On Zerosoft Cloud you start on a free plan and, if you scale, pay for usage, with transparent prices. Software was never the expensive part; the business model was.

f2.q: Can I migrate my links from Bitly?
f2.a: Yes. Paste your Bitly API token to import the whole account, or upload Bitly's CSV export — up to 2,000 links per run, back-halves included. Add and verify your custom domain here first: once you move the DNS, the same links keep working.

f3.q: What happens if Zerosoft shuts down?
f3.a: Nothing bad. The code is open source, so anyone can run it forever. Export every link as CSV and every click as JSON whenever you want. Your links can never be held hostage.

f4.a: That is the point. The core is AGPLv3: run it on any server with Node and SQLite, set your own domain, done. No license key, no phone-home, every core feature included. Only enterprise extras (SSO, audit logs) come under a commercial license.

f5.a: Only if you tell them to. Links never expire on their own and never get parked behind a paywall. Expiration is a feature you control, not a threat we use.

cta.sub: Free, open, already live. Your first short link is ten seconds away.

s1.d: One link, or up to 200 at once. Already on Bitly? Import your links through its API or a CSV.

s2.d: Pick the alias, use your own domain, add UTM tags, a QR code, a password, an expiry date or a click limit.

s3.d: Cookie-less analytics by day, referrer, country, device, browser and OS. Export to CSV or fire a webhook on every click.

meta.title: Track — Project management at zero
meta.description: Issues, cycles and timelines with the speed of Linear, without the $8 per head. Open source. Live now.

hero.sub: Issues, cycles and timelines in the spirit of Linear — without the $8 per head. Board, list, calendar and Gantt. Open source. Live now.

f1.d: Board, list, calendar and Gantt. Same issues, the shape your day needs.

f2.d: Work in focused one or two-week cycles. Scope, ship, review, repeat.

f3.d: Every issue with dates on a Gantt timeline the whole team can read.

f4.d: Break work down, mark blockers and duplicates. The graph behind the board, visible.

f5.d: Mentions, assignments and updates in one place. Mark them read and get back to work.

f6.d: Custom statuses per project, priorities from low to urgent. Structure work your way.

f7.d: Point issues so everyone knows how big the work is before it starts.

f8.d: Filter by status, priority, assignee or cycle. Save the view, open it tomorrow.

f9.d: Every change on an issue, logged. Comment, mention, attach files. Nothing gets lost.

compare.note: Linear Standard costs $8 per user per month. A team of 10 pays $960 a year, every year, forever. Self-hosted Track costs $0.

f1.a: Yes. The core is open source under AGPLv3, so self-hosting costs nothing. Our hosted cloud starts with a free plan and then charges for usage, with transparent prices.

f2.a: Not automatically yet. A Linear importer is on the roadmap. Today you create projects and issues by hand — most teams start fresh with what matters.

f3.q: What happens if Zerosoft shuts down?
f3.a: You keep everything. The code is open and self-hosting takes one command, so your issues live on your database. There is no lock-in to lock you in.

f4.a: Absolutely. That is the default way to run every Zerosoft product: your server, your data, your rules. The cloud exists for those who would rather not run servers.

f5.a: Yes. Track is live: open it, create a project and ship your first issue today — for $0.

cta.sub: Track is live. Open it, create a project and move your first card today — for $0.

s1.d: Create a project with your own statuses and invite the team to the shared workspace.

s2.d: Issues with sub-issues, relations, priorities and estimates. Group them into cycles to plan each sprint.

s3.d: Follow progress on a list, board, calendar or Gantt timeline. Comments, activity and an inbox keep everyone in sync.

meta.title: CRM — Customers without the invoice

f1.d: Drag deals across stages you define. One pipeline or ten — no per-pipeline pricing.

f2.d: Every person, every company, every touchpoint in one place. Searchable in milliseconds.

f3.d: Connect Gmail and sync your conversations with each contact in one click. They land on the right timeline.

f4.d: Calls, meetings, notes and tasks on a timeline per deal. Meetings booked in Cal land there on their own.

f5.d: Pipeline value, conversion by stage, forecast by month. The numbers your Monday meeting needs.

f6.d: CSV in, CSV out. From HubSpot, Pipedrive, or a spreadsheet named final_final2.

f7.d: Invite your team into one workspace. Everyone sees the same pipeline. Granular roles are coming soon.

f8.d: When a deal changes stage, create a task, send an email or notify the owner. Simple rules, zero consultants.

f9.d: A REST API for contacts, companies, deals, activities and tasks, plus signed webhooks when contacts and deals change. It is your data.

compare.note: HubSpot Sales Hub Professional starts near $50 per user per month. Ten salespeople: $6,000 a year — before onboarding fees. Self-hosted CRM costs $0.

f1.a: Yes. The core is open source (AGPLv3) and self-hosting costs nothing. On Zerosoft Cloud you start on a free plan and, if you scale, pay for usage, with transparent prices. We sell convenience, never the core.

f2.a: Yes, for your contacts and companies: export them from HubSpot as CSV and import them, mapping each column to a field. Deals are created in the pipeline you set up here.

f3.q: What happens if Zerosoft shuts down?
f3.a: Nothing, for you. The code is open, your data is exportable at any moment, and the self-hosted version keeps running no matter what happens to us.

f4.a: Yes — it is the point of the project. Your customer data is probably the most sensitive data you have; keeping it on your own server is a feature, not a chore.

f5.a: It already did. CRM is live: open it, import your contacts and close your first deal today — for $0, obviously.

s1.d: Import contacts and companies from any CSV, mapping each column to a field, with duplicates detected for you.

s2.d: Move deals across the stages of one or several pipelines on a kanban board. Log calls, notes and tasks on each timeline.

s3.d: Workflows send emails, create tasks or call webhooks when something changes. Reports and dashboards show where the money is.

meta.title: Cal — Scheduling, set free
meta.description: Your availability as a link. Google Calendar sync, timezone detection, round-robin, embeds and an API — without $12 a month. Open source. Live now.

hero.sub: Your availability as a link. People pick a slot, it lands in your Google Calendar, everyone gets the invite, and nobody pays $12 a month for the privilege. Live now.

f1.d: One link per meeting: zerosoft.ai/book/you/30min. Days with nothing free are disabled. On desktop, calendar and slots side by side.

f2.d: Busy in Google means busy here. Every booking lands in your calendar, with a Google Meet link when there is no other location. Reschedule or cancel and it updates.

f3.d: Guests see their timezone, you see yours. Padding before and after, minimum notice, custom questions. Your calendar, defended.

f4.d: Ask a few questions, send each person to the right event type, spread bookings across the team. Each host connects their own Google Calendar.

f5.d: Cancel or reschedule from the link in the email. No account, no back and forth.

f6.d: Confirmation, reschedule and cancel emails carry an .ics invite. A reminder 24 hours before, with the manage link. No-shows drop.

f7.d: Put it inline on any site — it sizes itself — or behind a popup button.

f8.d: REST API v1 for event types and bookings: list, create, get, cancel. booking.created, booking.rescheduled and booking.cancelled as signed webhooks, with retries.

f9.d: Availability is per person, across every event type. Two guests cannot grab the same slot, not even at the same second. Block holidays and focus time too.

compare.note: Calendly Standard costs about $12 per user per month. Ten people scheduling: $1,440 a year, every year. Self-hosted Cal costs $0.

f1.a: Yes. The core is open source, so self-hosting costs nothing. On Zerosoft Cloud you start on a free plan and, if you scale, pay for usage, with transparent prices. Scheduling is bits and a calendar API — it was never worth $12 a month.

f2.a: Recreating your event types takes minutes — durations, buffers and questions all map over. Connect Google Calendar, embed your new link where the old one was, done.

f3.q: What happens if Zerosoft shuts down?
f3.a: You would not notice. Self-host the same code on your server and your booking pages keep working on your domain.

f4.a: Yes. Run the core, set your availability, share your link. No license server, no premium tier hiding the good parts: the whole core is yours. Only enterprise extras (SSO, audit logs, white-label) come under a commercial license.

f5.q: Does it sync with my calendar?
f5.a: Google Calendar, yes: busy times block your slots and every booking lands in your calendar with a Meet link. Outlook and iCloud are coming soon.

cta.sub: Cal is live. Create an event type and share your link today — for $0.

s1.d: Set the duration, the questions you need answered, your weekly availability, buffers and minimum notice.

s2.d: Send your booking link or embed it on your site, inline or as a popup. Round-robin spreads meetings across the team.

s3.d: The meeting lands in Google Calendar with a Meet link. Everyone gets the invite and a 24h reminder; guests can reschedule or cancel on their own.

f5.d: Invite your whole company. Self-hosted, the price stays at $0 no matter how many people read.

f6.d: Every page is stored as clean JSON in your own database. One-click export is coming soon.

f7.d: Find pages by title in milliseconds. The search you actually need, not the one you pay extra for.

f9.d: Your documents stay on your server if you want them to. No vendor lock-in, ever.

meta.title: Chat — Customer support, set free
meta.description: An Intercom-style support desk: webchat widget, shared inbox, ticket states and priority, SLAs, auto-answer bot, office hours and CSAT. Open source. Live now.

hero.sub: An Intercom-style support desk: webchat widget, shared inbox, ticket states and priority, SLAs, an auto-answer bot, office hours and CSAT. Open source. Live now.

f1.d: One script tag puts a fast, monochrome chat widget on any site. Identify visitors and greet them by name.

f2.d: Every conversation lands in one inbox the whole team works: assign, reply, snooze, resolve. No forwarding, no BCC.

f3.d: Open, pending, resolved — with priorities from low to urgent that bubble the important ones up. Nothing slips.

f4.d: Set first-response and resolution targets and see what is about to breach before it does. Support with a clock.

f5.d: The bot matches keywords against your canned responses and docs pages, answers the repetitive questions first, and hands off to a human with the full thread.

f6.d: Show an away message with your expected response time when you're off, and measure satisfaction (1–5) when a conversation is resolved.

f7.d: Route conversations to the right teammate automatically and answer in two keystrokes with saved replies.

f8.d: Every visitor, lead and customer in one place: who they are, what they saw, what they asked.

f9.d: Support is a team sport. Open source and self-hostable: invite everyone, the price stays $0.

compare.note: Intercom starts around $29 per seat per month. A team of ten pays $3,480 a year. Self-hosted Chat costs $0.

f1.a: Yes. Open source (AGPLv3) and self-hostable for $0. On Zerosoft Cloud you start on a free plan and, if you scale, pay for usage, with transparent prices.

f2.q: How do I add the widget to my site?
f2.a: Create a widget, paste one script tag before the closing body tag, and you are live. It works with any stack that serves HTML.

f3.q: Does the bot replace my team?
f3.a: No. It answers repetitive questions by matching keywords against your canned responses and docs pages; your team keeps the conversations that need a human. You can turn it off entirely.

f4.q: What happens if Zerosoft shuts down?
f4.a: You keep your conversations. Self-host the same code and your support history stays in your own database.

f5.a: Chat is live now. Create your first widget and answer customers today — for $0.

cta.sub: Chat is live. Put the widget on your site today — for $0.

s1.d: Copy one script tag into your site. Visitors get a webchat that respects your office hours.

s2.d: Every conversation lands in a shared inbox, with states, priorities, assignment rules and SLA timers.

s3.d: Canned responses for the usual questions and an auto-answer bot that matches them by keyword. CSAT tells you how it went.

meta.title: Agents, open-source AI agents
meta.description: AI agents that answer from your own knowledge and use tools across CRM, Cal, Track and Flow. An open-source alternative to Intercom Fin.

hero.sub: AI agents that help your customers using your own knowledge and act across the suite: they save leads, book meetings and hand off to your team when needed.

f1.d: Describe what it does, how it talks and when it uses each tool, the way you would brief a new hire.

f2.d: It searches your Docs pages, up to 20 websites and your saved Chat replies.

f3.d: It saves leads to the CRM, offers times and books in Cal, files Track issues and runs flows.

f4.d: When the visitor asks or the agent is unsure, it alerts your team and stops replying.

f5.d: Your site’s Chat widget, a full-screen public page and an API for your own app.

f6.d: Test it before you publish, and every conversation records which tools it used and with what data.

compare.note: Intercom charges about $0.99 for every conversation Fin resolves, on top of Intercom seats. At 1,000 resolutions a month that is $11,880 a year. Agents on your server costs whatever your AI model uses.

f1.q: Which AI model does it use?
f1.a: Any model on the AI Gateway, written as provider/model (for example, anthropic/claude-sonnet-5-5). On your server, you pay for usage directly with your own key.

f2.a: It answers from your knowledge and, when unsure, hands off to a person. Every answer is logged with the tools it used, so you can review it.

f3.q: Where does it talk to my customers?
f3.a: In the Chat widget on your site, on its own public page and through the API from your app.

f4.a: Only with the tools you turn on, and only inside your workspace. To book a meeting it needs a time it offered itself and the visitor’s confirmation.

s2.d: Add Docs pages and websites, and turn on only the tools it needs.

s3.d: Connect it to the Chat widget, share its page or call it through the API.

meta.description: Visual automations across every zerosoft app and any API. An open-source alternative to Zapier and n8n.

hero.sub: Visual automations across every zerosoft app and any service with an API. Triggers, conditions, loops and AI steps on one canvas.

f1.d: A Cal booking, a Link click, a new contact, an issue or a Chat message.

f2.d: Start from a POST to a secret URL or every N minutes, in your time zone.

f3.d: Conditions, branches and loops over lists, on a canvas where you drag and connect nodes.

f4.d: Create contacts, enroll in sequences, open issues, reply in Chat and write to Docs.

f5.d: Summarize, classify or draft text in the middle of a flow.

f6.d: Every run keeps what went in and out of each node, so you find the error fast.

meta.title: Robots, open-source browser automation
meta.description: Robots that browse, fill in forms and extract data for you. An open-source alternative to UiPath.

hero.sub: Browser robots that visit pages, click, fill in forms and extract data for you. Run them by hand, on a schedule or from Flow.

f1.d: Open a URL, click, fill in, wait, extract text or tables and take screenshots.

f2.d: Define named values and the same robot works for another product or another page.

f3.d: It walks through lists of items and decides what to do based on what it finds.

f4.d: It runs every day at the time you choose, or by hand when you need it.

f5.d: A flow starts it, waits for the result and uses the data in the next step.

f6.d: Each run opens a fresh browser and closes it when done. On Vercel, inside a microVM.

compare.note: UiPath Basic starts at about $25 a month for up to 2 robots; Standard and Enterprise are quoted separately. Robots on your server costs $0; on Vercel you pay for the Sandbox minutes you use.

f1.a: A browser that follows steps: open a page, click, fill in fields, read text or tables and take screenshots. You build it step by step, without writing code.

f2.a: On your server with Chromium, or in an isolated Vercel Sandbox microVM if you deploy on Vercel.

f3.q: Does it work on sites with a login?
f3.a: Robots are meant for public pages. Inputs are stored in plain text and the whole workspace can see them, so do not store passwords.

f4.q: How do I use what it extracts?
f4.a: Every run returns JSON. From Flow you can create contacts, send an email or file an issue with that data.

cta.sub: Start from a template: read a table, track a price, fill in a form or take a screenshot.

s1.d: Start with Go to URL and add clicks, fields and extractions.

s2.d: Run it by hand and see what it extracted at each step.

s3.d: Give it a schedule or call it from a flow.

meta.title: API Docs — Zerosoft
meta.description: The Zerosoft REST API: links, CRM and Cal. Personal keys, JSON responses, zero friction.

docs.label: 0.05 — API
docs.title: The Zerosoft API.
docs.intro: All products expose the same style of API: REST, JSON and personal keys. If the dashboard can do it, your code can do it.
docs.authDesc: Every request needs an API key, sent as a Bearer token. For browser sessions the Google OAuth flow creates the session cookie.
docs.authNote: Create keys in Dashboard → Settings → API keys. A key is shown exactly once — copy it and store it like a password. Each key allows 100 requests per minute.
docs.linksDesc: Create, list, update and measure short links.
docs.authFlowDesc: Redirect the user to start the Google OAuth flow. After success they return to the app with a session cookie.
docs.linksCreateDesc: Creates a short link. slug is optional — leave it out and we generate one.
docs.linksListDesc: Your links, newest first. Paginate with page and pageSize (max 100).
docs.linksDeleteDesc: Archive or delete a link by id.
docs.linksPatchDesc: Update any writable field of a link.
docs.linksStatsDesc: Click totals and a per-day breakdown for one link.
docs.contactsListDesc: List contacts. Filters: q, page, pageSize (max 100).
docs.contactsPatchDesc: Update any property of a contact.
docs.companiesListDesc: List companies. Filters: q, page, pageSize.
docs.companiesPatchDesc: Update any property of a company.
docs.dealsCreateDesc: Create a deal in a pipeline stage.
docs.tasksListDesc: List tasks. bucket: overdue, today, upcoming, done.
docs.tasksCreateDesc: Create a task, optionally linked to a record.
docs.stagesCreateDesc: Create a stage inside a pipeline.
docs.teamsInviteDesc: Invite an email to join a team.
docs.teamsSwitchDesc: Switch active workspace. Use teamId: null for the personal workspace.
docs.docsPatchDesc: Update title, content or archive a page.
docs.paramTaskBucket: Filter bucket: overdue, today, upcoming, done.
docs.paramTeamIdSwitch: Team id or null for the personal workspace.
docs.calDesc: Event types and bookings. Bookings created through the API follow the same rules as the public page (availability, buffers, Google Calendar busy times) and send the same emails.
docs.calEventTypesDesc: Your event types with their public booking URL.
docs.calBookingsListDesc: Bookings of your event types, newest first. Filter by status and date range.
docs.calBookingsCreateDesc: Books a slot for a guest. Returns 409 slot_unavailable if the time isn't offered anymore.
docs.calBookingsGetDesc: One booking by id (event type owner or assigned host).
docs.calBookingsCancelDesc: Cancels a confirmed booking, emails the guest a cancellation with .ics, removes the Google Calendar event and emits booking.cancelled.
docs.agentsDesc: Talk to your AI agents from your own app. The agent uses the same instructions, knowledge and tools as in Chat and on its public page; every reply counts toward the workspace AI quota.
docs.agentsMessagesTitle: Send a message to an agent
docs.agentsMessagesDesc: Returns the agent's reply and the tools it used. Send the returned conversationId to continue the same conversation. Errors: 404 not_found, 403 agent_disabled, 429 rate_limited, 503 ai_disabled.
docs.paramAgentMessage: What the user says (up to 4000 characters).
docs.paramAgentConversationId: Continue an existing API conversation. Omit it to start a new one.
docs.webhooksDesc: Add endpoints in Dashboard → Settings → Webhooks. Events: booking.created, booking.rescheduled, booking.cancelled, link.created, link.clicked, contact.created, contact.updated, deal.created, deal.updated, deal.stage_changed, deal.won, deal.lost. Each request carries Zerosoft-Signature: t=TIMESTAMP,v1=HEX, where v1 = HMAC-SHA256(secret, "TIMESTAMP.RAW_BODY"). Reject old timestamps. Failed deliveries are retried with backoff for ~15 hours.
docs.webhooksPayloadDesc: What your endpoint receives. Respond 2xx within 8 seconds.
docs.paramCalEventTypeId: Event type id (from List event types).
docs.paramCalStart: Slot start, must match an offered slot.
docs.paramCalEmail: Guest email: receives the confirmation and calendar invite.
docs.paramCalTimezone: Guest timezone for the emails. Defaults to UTC.
docs.paramCalReason: Shown to the guest in the cancellation email.
docs.contactsDeleteDesc: Permanently deletes the contact. Its activities stay, unlinked.
docs.companiesDeleteDesc: Permanently deletes the company. Contacts keep existing without a company.
docs.dealsMoveTitle: Move a deal to a stage
docs.dealsMoveDesc: Moves the deal to another stage of its pipeline. Won/lost stages close it; a lost stage needs lostReason. Fires deal.stage_changed (and deal.won / deal.lost).
docs.crmActivitiesDesc: The timeline of a contact, company or deal: notes, calls, meetings, emails and tasks. Meetings booked in Cal show up here automatically.
docs.activitiesListDesc: Most recent first. Pass exactly one of contactId, companyId or dealId.
docs.activitiesCreateDesc: Log a note, call, meeting or email on a record. Tasks have their own endpoint.
docs.paramContactIds: IDs of the contacts to enroll (1–500).
docs.paramLostReason: Why it was lost (required for lost stages).
docs.paramRecordFilter: The record whose timeline you want.
docs.paramActivityBody: Free text: notes, call summary, email body.
docs.crmEmailDesc: Shared email templates and snippets, and multi-step sales sequences. Sequence emails are sent from the sender's connected Gmail; steps run on the hourly scheduler.
docs.emailTemplatesListDesc: Templates and snippets shared in the workspace. Variables go between double curly braces (contact.first_name, contact.company, deal.name, owner.first_name, contact.custom.x), with an optional fallback after a pipe.
docs.sequencesListDesc: Sequences with their number of steps and enrollments.
docs.sequencesEnrollDesc: Enrolls up to 500 contacts. Contacts that are already enrolled, unsubscribed or without email are returned in skipped. The sender needs Gmail connected with send permission.
docs.sequencesUnenrollDesc: Removes the contact from the sequence (status exited, reason manual).
docs.paramTemplateKind: Filter by kind: template or snippet.
docs.paramSenderId: Workspace member whose Gmail sends the emails. Defaults to the contact owner, then the sequence creator.
docs.crmProductsDesc: Product catalog and the line items of each deal. While a deal has line items, its amount is the sum of their net totals (after discount, before tax) unless amountOverride is on.
docs.crmQuotesDesc: Quotes created from a deal's line items. Each quote keeps a snapshot of the items and has a public page (public_url) where the customer accepts or declines. Accepting fires the Flow event quote.accepted and the quote_accepted workflow trigger.
docs.crmAssociationsDesc: Many-to-many links between contacts, companies and deals. A contact or deal can have several companies; one of them is primary. contact.company_id always mirrors the primary company.
docs.crmTagsDesc: Workspace tags for contacts, companies and deals.
docs.productsListDesc: Products in the catalog, active first, sorted by name.
docs.productsCreateDesc: Adds a product to the catalog. Without currency it uses the workspace base currency.
docs.productsPatchDesc: Updates the fields you send. Line items already on deals don't change.
docs.productsDeleteDesc: Deletes the product. Line items that used it stay on their deals as custom items.
docs.lineItemsListDesc: Line items with their computed subtotal, discount, net, tax and total, plus the deal totals. Amounts are rounded per line to the deal currency.
docs.lineItemsCreateDesc: From a product (copies name, price, tax and recurrence; the price is converted to the deal currency when there is an exchange rate) or custom (name and unitPrice). Recalculates the deal amount.
docs.lineItemsPatchDesc: Updates quantity, price, discount, tax or text and recalculates the deal amount.
docs.lineItemsDeleteDesc: Removes the line item and recalculates the deal amount.
docs.quotesListDesc: Quotes of the workspace, newest first. Sent quotes past their expiration date are returned as expired.
docs.quotesCreateDesc: Creates a draft quote from the deal's current line items (the deal needs at least one). Defaults: expires in 30 days, recipient = first contact and primary company of the deal.
docs.quotesGetDesc: Returns the quote with its items and public_url.
docs.quotesPatchDesc: Edits a draft. status: "sent" publishes the public link (draft → sent). Accepting and declining happen on the public page. Non-draft quotes answer 409 not_draft.
docs.associationsListDesc: All records linked to a contact, company or deal. Companies also return their parent and child companies.
docs.associationsCreateDesc: Links contact ↔ company, deal ↔ company or deal ↔ contact (in either order). primary makes the company the primary one; label only applies to contact ↔ company. Linking an existing association updates its primary flag and label.
docs.associationsDeleteDesc: Unlinks two records (query parameters). Removing the primary company promotes the oldest remaining one.
docs.tagsListDesc: Tags with how many contacts, companies and deals use each one.
docs.tagsCreateDesc: Names are unique per workspace (case-insensitive). A duplicate answers 409 duplicate_tag.
docs.tagsPatchDesc: Renames the tag or changes its color.
docs.tagsDeleteDesc: Deletes the tag and removes it from every record.
docs.tagsRecordsDesc: Adds or removes the tag on up to 1000 records. Ids from other workspaces are ignored. Returns how many records changed.
docs.paramParentCompanyId: Parent company id (hierarchy). null makes it top-level. A company can't be its own ancestor.
docs.paramPrimaryCompanyId: Primary company id. It's associated if needed; the previous primary stays associated. null removes the primary.
docs.paramDealCompanyIds: Other companies to associate with the deal.
docs.paramAmountOverride: true keeps a manual amount even with line items; false recalculates it from the line items. Editing amount on a deal with line items turns it on.
docs.paramProductActiveFilter: true = active only, false = archived only.
docs.paramProductDescription: Description shown on line items and quotes.
docs.paramProductCurrency: ISO currency code (defaults to the workspace base currency).
docs.paramProductActive: false archives the product (hidden from pickers).
docs.paramRecurring: Billing interval: none, monthly or yearly.
docs.paramLineProductId: Catalog product id. Omit it for a custom line item.
docs.paramLineName: Line item name (required for custom items).
docs.paramUnitPrice: Unit price in the deal currency.
docs.paramQuoteDealId: Deal whose line items become the quote.
docs.paramQuoteTitle: Quote title (defaults to the deal name).
docs.paramQuoteSender: Sender details shown on the quote.
docs.paramQuoteRecipient: Recipient details (default: the deal's first contact and primary company).
docs.paramQuoteRefresh: Re-snapshot the deal's current line items (drafts only).
docs.paramAssocType: Record type: contact, company or deal.
docs.paramAssocPrimary: Make this the primary company of the contact or deal.
docs.paramAssocLabel: Contact ↔ company label: employee, decision_maker, billing, champion, influencer, former_employee (or empty).
docs.paramTagColor: Color: crm, link, cal, track, chat, docs, flow, agents, notes, board or robots.
docs.paramTagEntity: Record type: contact, company or deal.
docs.scopesIntro: Every key has scopes, chosen when you create it. Write scopes include read. Keys created before scopes existed have all of them. A request without the needed scope gets 403 insufficient_scope.
docs.scopesVisibility: A key acts as the person who created it: if your workspace limits members to their own (or their team’s) CRM records, the API returns only those records.
docs.scope_crm_read: Read contacts, companies, deals, activities, tasks, pipelines, products, quotes, tags, templates, sequences and forms.
docs.scope_crm_write: Create, update and delete CRM records, enroll in sequences, tag records (includes crm:read).
docs.scope_links_read: List links and read their stats.
docs.scope_links_write: Create, update and delete short links (includes links:read).
docs.scope_agents_run: Send messages to your AI agents.
docs.crmFormsDesc: Lead capture forms and their submissions. Each submission also creates or updates a contact and logs a "Form submitted" activity.
docs.formsListDesc: All forms in the workspace with their fields, status and submission count. `key` is the public slug (or token) used in /f/'<key>' and the embed script.
docs.formsSubmissionsDesc: Submissions of a form, newest first, with the submitted values, UTM parameters and the linked contact.
